page-A.html.primary_focus_finding: NO. A teacher scanning page A does not find one clear primary focus. The page's own comments declare a primary/secondary split, but the classes carrying it do not exist in the system: .oak-btn-primary and .oak-btn-secondary (single hyphen) are undefined, while the shipped modifier is .oak-btn--secondary (double hyphen, components.css:328) and bare .oak-btn IS the filled primary face (components.css:271-293). All ten buttons on the page therefore render identically as filled primaries - the hero CTA, eight 'View lesson' buttons stacked down the main column, and 'Download all resources'. The wall of equal visual weight the brief asked to cure is reproduced in a new form.

type-scale-usage.note: Three separate defects. (1) A class the system does not define: the hero teaser at line 207 uses .oak-body, but the shipped families are .oak-body-1 through .oak-body-4 plus -bold variants (verified across all five system CSS files) - so the page's one-line unit subtitle renders with no type style at all. (2) Text with no type class: every .lesson-row__desc (lines 233, 241, 249, ...) carries only a layout class, so eight lesson descriptions render at browser default rather than the system's supporting-text style. (3) Raw sizing off the scale: .related__heading 0.875rem with text-transform uppercase and 0.04em tracking (line 152-154), .related-card__title 0.9375rem (line 175), .related-card__meta 0.8125rem (line 180), .downloads-list li 0.9375rem (line 136). The system scale is 0.75/0.875/1/1.125/1.25/1.5/2/2.5/3/3.5rem - 0.9375rem (15px) and 0.8125rem (13px) are not steps on it. Separately, one style carries two roles: .oak-heading-5 is used for both the h3 lesson titles (line 232) and the h2 sidebar panel headings (lines 300, 311), so a rank-2 and a rank-3 heading render identically.

spatial-rhythm.note: No spacing on the page comes from the token scale. Every value is written as var(--oak-space-N, <rem>), and no --oak-space-* token exists anywhere in the system - I checked all seventeen names used (--oak-space-1 through --oak-space-14, --oak-radius-2) against colors_and_type.css, components.css, brand.css, oak-icons.css and print.css: zero definitions. The rem fallbacks are what actually render, so the whole rhythm is raw and unrelated to the system's --space-* scale. Same for --oak-radius-2 (the system ships --radius-container). Additional raw values: .lesson-row__number width/height 2.25rem and border-radius 999px where --radius-circle ships (colors_and_type.css:168), and a 1px card border where --border-solid-m is 2px (colors_and_type.css:153). The header comment states the fallbacks are 'conservative' insurance for unresolved names; in practice every single name is unresolved, so the insurance is the design.

hierarchy.note: The heading outline itself is sound - h1 (line 206) to h2 (line 227) to h3 (line 232), no skips, and DOM order matches visual order with the 2fr main column preceding the 1fr aside. The failure is that rendered prominence does not track meaning. First: the primary/secondary button distinction does not exist on screen. .oak-btn-primary and .oak-btn-secondary are not classes the system defines; the shipped names are bare .oak-btn (filled primary, components.css:282-284) and .oak-btn--secondary (quiet outline, components.css:328-332). So the hero CTA and all eight 'View lesson' buttons and the sidebar download button all render as full-weight filled primaries - eight identical high-emphasis buttons marching down the main column, which is the exact 'everything at the same visual weight' condition the brief named. Second: .oak-heading-5 is shared by the h3 lesson titles and the h2 sidebar panel headings, so a supporting sidebar heading is as loud as the primary content's item titles. Third: because the page overrides .oak-card in its own style block (see composition-grammar), the system's signature accent shadow that would have marked the card set is removed, so shadow carries no emphasis signal either. The result is a page whose intent is legible in the source comments and not on the render.

colour-discipline.note: Every colour on the page is a raw literal. The seven token names used (--oak-color-grey-01/02/03/06, --oak-color-white, --oak-color-teal-50, --oak-color-teal-90) have zero definitions in the system, so what renders is the fallback hex: #f7f7f7 (body, line 18), #e0e0e0 (all borders), #fff (cards and lesson rows), #dff1ee and #1b4d46 (lesson number chip, lines 94-95), #595959 (secondary text), #eee (download row rules). The consequence is larger than the literals: the page is theme-blind. The system overrides the semantic tier at :root, with --text-primary: light-dark(var(--oak-black), var(--oak-white)) (colors_and_type.css:277). Under data-theme='dark' the lesson rows and sidebar cards keep their hardcoded #fff background while their text inherits --text-primary, which resolves to white - white text on white cards throughout the main column and sidebar. Contrast floors do hold in the default light cell judged (#595959 on #fff is about 7:1), so the failure is the literals and the theme break, not the light-mode ratios.

composition-grammar.note: The page uses none of the export's region model. No .oak-scope on body, no .oak-canvas, no [data-page] map, no .oak-main, no [data-region] sections, no .oak-container, no .oak-band - .page, .hero, .unit-grid, .sidebar and .related are improvised where components.css:1225-1350 ships all of them, and where the export's own composed page (studio-source/ui_kits/oak/index.html:49-72) demonstrates masthead / main(hero, featured, content, context, cta) / footer. There is no masthead and no footer region at all. Landmark structure is also improvised: the hero and the related-units strip sit OUTSIDE <main>, which contains only the lesson list. Most seriously for containment, the page's own <style> block re-declares the SYSTEM class .oak-card (lines 114-119, setting background, border, border-radius, padding). It loads after styles.css at equal specificity, so it wins - the shipped card's box-shadow: var(--shadow-accent) and color: var(--text-primary) are silently dropped for every card on the page, and any other consumer of .oak-card on the same document is mutated too. There is also an inline style="width:100%; text-align:center;" on line 318, bypassing the token system.

cross-page-cohesion.note: Judged against the export's own composed specimens, which are the system this page set has to read as one with. A reader arriving from any page built on the region model meets a different architecture (no masthead, no footer, no canvas/main maps, no containers, no bands), a different card face (bespoke .lesson-row at 1px #e0e0e0 with no shadow, plus a globally overridden .oak-card that has lost the accent shadow) and a control vocabulary that collapses to a single button face because the secondary modifier name is wrong. Same-role elements would diverge in every one of those dimensions. The type vocabulary also diverges: two off-scale sizes (15px, 13px) and one nonexistent class (.oak-body) that no sibling page could share.

ordered-calm-readability.note: No overlap or collage anywhere, no rotation of any kind, no page-authored motion (no keyframes and no page-level transitions). The layout is a plain two-column grid over a linear list. The related-units strip uses overflow-x: auto, but four cards at 11-14rem inside a 76rem page do not overflow at desktop, so nothing is hidden off-screen in the judged cell. One note applying equally to both pages: the kit's own components ship interaction motion (.oak-btn transition, components.css:288-290) - that is the export's stance question, not something this page introduced.

page-B.html.primary_focus_finding: YES. A teacher scanning page B finds one clear primary focus, and three independent channels agree on it. Heading size: 'Lessons in this unit' at .oak-heading-3 (40px) is the largest content heading, against 'About this unit' and 'Downloads' at .oak-heading-5 (24px) and 'More units' at .oak-heading-6 (20px). Shadow weight: the six lesson cards carry the system's signature accent shadow (the .oak-card default, components.css:468), Downloads carries .oak-card--grey-shadow, related units carry .oak-card--flat with no shadow at all. Band tone: the closing related strip sits in a --bg-subtle band that visually ends the page. The hero gives exactly one named next action ('Start with lesson 1', primary face) against one secondary ('Get all resources'), so the top of the page points into the primary set rather than competing with it.

type-scale-usage.note: Text renders through composite styles throughout - .oak-heading-1/3/5/6, .oak-body-1/2/3/4 and the -bold variants, all verified present in colors_and_type.css - and where a class was not appropriate the page uses the composite type-style tokens directly (font: var(--type-body-3) on .crumb-list, var(--type-body-4) on .lesson-chip), which is the dtcg type-style source form. One style per role, and hierarchy is expressed through the scale. Single deviation to note: .lesson-num (line 108) hand-assembles font: var(--weight-bold) var(--font-size-4) / 1 var(--font-sans) from primitives rather than using a composite type style, with a raw 1 for line-height. The size and weight are both on-scale so this is not a fail condition, but it is the one place the page reaches past the composite tier.

spatial-rhythm.note: All spacing comes from the --space-* scale and --gap-l, verified defined. The rhythm is deliberate and consistent: the shipped --main-gap is 0 var(--gap-l), i.e. zero row gap by design, so regions must supply their own vertical space - the page gives the three unbanded sibling regions one shared .oak-region-pad of var(--space-48) while the two banded regions take --band-pad, so every sibling separation is one of two recorded steps. Three notes, none reaching a fail condition. (1) Raw ch measures: max-width 20ch on .hero-title and 60ch on .hero-teaser where --measure-prose (65ch) ships. (2) A raw @media (max-width: 760px) for .unit-summary-grid that disagrees with the system's own narrow breakpoint of 840px (components.css:1337) - between 761px and 840px the summary grid is still two-up while the main map has already gone narrow. (3) .related-grid restates the shipped .oak-grid default with a raw 240px, but .oak-grid already declares repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(var(--space-240), 100%), 1fr)) and --space-240 IS 240px - so the override changes nothing and swaps a token for a literal.

hierarchy.note: One primary focus, and the spine descends monotonically without a break: hero h1 .oak-heading-1 (56px) in a tone band, then 'Lessons in this unit' h2 .oak-heading-3 (40px) over six accent-shadow cards, then 'About this unit' h2 .oak-heading-5 (24px), then 'Downloads' h2 .oak-heading-5 (24px) in a grey-shadow card, then 'More units' h2 .oak-heading-6 (20px) in --text-subdued over flat cards in a quiet closing band. Heading ranks descend without skips (h1, then h2 per section, then h3 per card) and reading order equals visual order because the map is single-column. Prominence tracks importance on three agreeing channels - type size, shadow weight, band tone - so the demotion of the summary and downloads below the lesson list is legible without reading a word. One thing to watch, not a fault: the hero band with a 56px title is the single loudest element on the page and sits above the declared primary scan target; the demotion holds only because the lessons own the largest content heading and the only accent shadows. If the hero grew another primary-faced action that balance would tip.

colour-discipline.note: Zero raw colour literals. Every colour arrives through a semantic role (--text-primary, --text-subdued, --bg-subtle, --border-primary, --surface-decorative-1, --surface-decorative-4-subtle) or through kit-class-carried colour, and all were verified defined. The tier direction is correct where it matters most: the page re-points COMPONENT tokens at SEMANTIC tokens rather than reaching for palette values - .hero-band sets --band-bg: var(--surface-decorative-4-subtle) and --band-border: var(--border-solid-m) solid var(--border-primary); .support-band sets --band-bg: var(--bg-subtle). Those are the hooks .oak-band exists to expose (components.css:179-184), so the page follows the themes rather than fighting them: under data-theme='high-contrast' both decorative surfaces resolve to --oak-white and the hero still delineates because the border was set to a role rather than left transparent. In the cell judged (default light) --oak-pink30 and --oak-mint under --oak-black text hold their floors comfortably. Roles are used for their meaning - decorative surfaces for bands and the number chip, --text-subdued for supporting text only.

composition-grammar.note: The full region model, used as shipped: .oak-scope on body, skip link, .oak-canvas carrying data-page, .oak-main with [data-region] sections in canonical order (hero, results, content, resources, support) and a sibling [data-region='footer'], .oak-container inside each region, .oak-band for the two tone regions, and .oak-stack / .oak-cluster / .oak-grid / .oak-card / .oak-card-link / .oak-icon-btn / .oak-block / .oak-key-learning-points from the kit - every class verified present. data-page sits on the canvas, exactly where the shipped comment says maps belong ('on <body> or the canvas, never at :root'). Nothing free-floats; every component sits inside a region and a container. Two notes. (1) The minted [data-page='unit-landing'] map is redundant: the universal fallback already stacks every region name in canonical order, and this page's five regions appear in that same relative order, so the mint produces exactly what the default would have produced. The reasoning for not reusing [data-page='unit'] is sound - that map is a facets/results browse shape - but the honest conclusion was to add no map at all. (2) No masthead region, where the export's own composed page carries one (studio-source/ui_kits/oak/index.html:49); the canvas's masthead row simply collapses.

cross-page-cohesion.note: Judged against the export's composed specimens as the sibling set. The page speaks the same grammar - same canvas and main maps, same region names, same container discipline - and uses kit control faces for their roles rather than inventing any: primary .oak-btn against .oak-btn--secondary, .oak-icon-btn--secondary for the per-row download affordance, .oak-tag--pink for the subject and .oak-tag--white for the neutral facts, one card family differentiated only by shipped shadow modifiers. All ten referenced icon assets resolve against assets/icons/. Two notes. (1) No masthead, so a sibling page carrying one would open differently. (2) Lesson-card titles use .oak-heading-6 while related-card titles use .oak-body-1-bold - defensible as a rank demotion (20px to 18px, and the related set is deliberately the quietest thing on the page), but it does mean two card-title roles in one page draw from different families, which a sibling page would have to reproduce consistently.

ordered-calm-readability.note: Single-column, strictly ordered composition. No overlap, no collage, no rotation of any kind anywhere on the page, and no page-authored motion - no keyframes, no animation, no page-level transition declarations. Density is even and the content is separated by bands and consistent padding rather than by visual trickery. One note applying equally to both pages: the kit's own components ship interaction motion (.oak-btn transition at components.css:288-290, and .oak-card-link:active transform: translate() at components.css:503-505, which this page inherits by using .oak-card-link). That is the export's stance to settle, not a page-authored addition.
